title: SDDC Manager credential sweep that survives an access-token expiry
prompt:
The `vcfsddc` Go module in this workspace is meant to sweep the credential inventory of a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager, but only the fixture, the protected checks and the README exist so far. Build the rest.

The sweep runs longer than an SDDC Manager access token lives. Part way through paging the inventory the token expires, and the sweep has to pick up a fresh access token and carry on from the page that was refused — without signing in again, without re-fetching pages it already has, and without skipping any.

Do not modify `verification/`, `scripts/verify.sh` or `testdata/credentials.json`. Use the standard library only: the checks run with the module proxy switched off, so a third-party dependency will not resolve.

## 1. Pin the contract in `docs/contract.json`

Derive it from the SDDC Manager OpenAPI document VMware publishes:

* repository `vmware/vcf-api-specs`
* file `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json`
* at tag `9.0.0.0` — not `main`, and not the 9.1 revision of the same file

Fetch that document and read the values out of it. Do not work from an HTML API reference page or from memory; the values below come from the specification document itself. The contract names three operations and nothing else: `createToken`, `refreshAccessToken` and `getCredentials`.

`docs/contract.json` is decoded strictly — a field name outside this shape is an error, so use exactly these names:

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "repository": "<owner/repo>",
    "path": "<the document's path inside that repository>",
    "tag": "<the tag>",
    "commit": "<the 40-character commit sha that tag points at, lower case>",
    "openapi": "<the document's top-level openapi field>",
    "title": "<the document's info.title>",
    "version": "<the document's info.version>"
  },
  "operations": [
    {
      "operationId": "<...>",
      "method": "<HTTP method, upper case>",
      "path": "<the path as written in the document, including its version prefix>",
      "successStatus": 200,
      "responseSchema": "<component schema name of that response's application/json body, or the body's type when it is not a $ref>",
      "requestBody": {
        "required": true,
        "contentType": "<the media type>",
        "schema": "<component schema name of the body, or the body's type when it is not a $ref>",
        "properties": ["<the body schema's property names, in document order>"]
      },
      "queryParameters": [
        {
          "name": "<...>",
          "required": false,
          "deprecated": true,
          "default": "<the parameter schema's default>",
          "allowedValues": ["<...>"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules for filling it in:

* `successStatus` is the operation's single 2xx response code, as a number.
* `requestBody` is omitted entirely for an operation that takes no body. `properties` is an empty list when the body is not an object.
* `queryParameters` is omitted entirely for an operation that takes none, and otherwise lists every query parameter of that operation in document order.
* `deprecated` is omitted when the parameter is not deprecated; `default` is omitted when the parameter schema has none.
* `allowedValues` appears only on the parameter whose accepted values the document enumerates, listed in the order the document gives them.

## 2. Record the source in `docs/official_sources.json`

```json
{
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "<what the document is>",
      "url": "<https link into the repository>",
      "repository": "<owner/repo>",
      "license": "<the repository's SPDX license identifier>",
      "path": "<the document's path>",
      "tag": "<the tag>",
      "commit": "<the commit sha>",
      "operationIds": ["<the operations the contract names>"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Exactly one entry. `url` must pin the commit sha rather than a branch or a tag, and must end with the document's path. `repository`, `path`, `tag` and `commit` must agree with `spec` in `docs/contract.json`.

## 3. `pkg/mock` — a loopback mock pinned to that contract

```go
package mock

type Config struct {
    ContractPath   string // docs/contract.json, the contract the server is pinned to
    FixturePath    string // the JSON array of credentials the server pages over
    Username       string // the only username createToken accepts
    Password       string // the only password createToken accepts
    AccessToken    string // the access token createToken hands out
    RefreshedToken string // the access token refreshAccessToken hands out
    RefreshTokenID string // the refresh token id createToken hands out and refreshAccessToken expects back
    ExpireAfter    int    // how many getCredentials requests are answered while bearing AccessToken
}

type Request struct {
    Index       int         // position in the log
    OperationID string      // the contract operation the request matched, "" when it matched none
    Method      string
    Path        string
    RawQuery    string
    Header      http.Header
    Body        []byte
    Status      int         // the status the server answered with
}

type Server struct{ /* ... */ }

func New(cfg Config) (*Server, error) // starts the server
func (s *Server) URL() string         // http://127.0.0.1:<port>
func (s *Server) Requests() []Request // the log, in arrival order
func (s *Server) Close()
```

* `New` binds an ephemeral port on the loopback interface, reads the contract and the fixture, and reports an error if either is missing or if `ContractPath`, `FixturePath`, `AccessToken`, `RefreshedToken` or `RefreshTokenID` is empty.
* Routing comes from the contract: only the method-and-path pairs it names are served. Anything else is `404`, logged with an empty `OperationID`.
* Every request is logged, whatever the outcome. `Requests` returns a snapshot the caller cannot use to mutate the server's copy.
* Failures answer with the specification's `Error` schema.
* `createToken`: a `Content-Type` other than the contract's media type is `400`; a body carrying a field outside the contract's property list for that body is `400`; a username or password other than `Config`'s is `400`. Otherwise `201` with a `TokenPair` carrying `Config.AccessToken` and `Config.RefreshTokenID`.
* `refreshAccessToken`: a `Content-Type` other than the contract's media type is `400`; a body that does not decode as the contract's request body schema is `400`; an unknown refresh token id is `404`. Otherwise `200` carrying `Config.RefreshedToken` encoded as the contract's response schema for that operation.
* `getCredentials`, in this order:
  1. A missing, malformed or unrecognised `Bearer` token is `401`. `Config.RefreshedToken` is always accepted. `Config.AccessToken` is accepted for the first `ExpireAfter` requests that present it and is `401` (`errorCode` `TOKEN_EXPIRED`) from then on.
  2. A query parameter the contract does not list for this operation is `400`; a repeated parameter is `400`; a parameter present with an empty value is `400`; a `pageNumber` or `pageSize` that is not a non-negative integer is `400`.
  3. Otherwise filter the fixture — `resourceType`, `resourceName` and `accountType` match exactly, `domainName` matches when it is one of the credential's `domainNames` — keeping fixture order, and return the requested page as a `PageOfCredential`. Its `pageMetadata` carries `pageNumber`, `pageSize` (the number of elements on this page), `totalElements` and `totalPages`. An absent or zero `pageSize` means a single page holding everything; `totalPages` is `0` when nothing matched.

## 4. `pkg/client` — the SDDC Manager client

```go
package client

type Config struct {
    BaseURL    string
    Username   string
    Password   string
    HTTPClient *http.Client // optional
}

type Filter struct { // every field optional
    ResourceName string
    ResourceType string
    DomainName   string
    AccountType  string
    PageSize     int
}

type Resource struct {
    ResourceID   string
    ResourceName string
    ResourceType string
    DomainNames  []string
}

type Credential struct {
    ID             string
    CredentialType string
    AccountType    string
    Username       string
    Resource       Resource
}

type Client struct{ /* ... */ }

func New(cfg Config) (*Client, error)
func (c *Client) ListCredentials(ctx context.Context, f Filter) ([]Credential, error)
```

* `New` rejects an empty `BaseURL`, `Username` or `Password`.
* `ListCredentials` signs in with `createToken` the first time it needs a token, then pages `getCredentials` from page 0 until the last page `pageMetadata.totalPages` reports, returning the elements in the order the API gave them.
* When a page comes back `401`, refresh the access token once with `refreshAccessToken` — sending the refresh token id `createToken` returned — and repeat that same page with the new token. If the refresh fails, or the repeat is refused as well, return an error. `createToken` is never called a second time.

## Request wire shape

* `pageNumber` is always sent. `pageSize` is sent only when `Filter.PageSize` is greater than zero. `resourceName`, `resourceType`, `domainName` and `accountType` are sent only when the corresponding field is non-empty. An unset optional parameter is left out of the query string entirely — never sent with an empty value.
* The `createToken` body is a JSON object carrying only the fields actually being used. The credential kinds the client is not using must not appear in the body at all, not even as empty strings.
* `Content-Type` is exactly `application/json`, and only on requests that carry a body.
* `createToken` carries no `Authorization` header and no query string.

## Tests

Write table-driven tests in `pkg/client` and `pkg/mock` covering, at least, the query strings the client builds, the body it sends to `createToken`, the recovery from an expired token, and the mock's routing, paging, filtering and rejection paths.

`./scripts/verify.sh` must pass. It checks the deliverables are present and the protected files untouched, then runs `go vet` and `go test -race` over the module with the module proxy off. Everything it exercises is local — the mock binds to 127.0.0.1 and no VMware endpoint is contacted.
